newsitem.title: USA: Japan allows imports of U.S. lumber.
newsitem.headline: Japan allows imports of U.S. lumber.

text.p: Japan has begun to allow importation of U.S.-grademarked lumber, the U.S. Trade Representative's office said Monday.

The move followed a 1990 bilateral agreement on market access for wood products, which calls for progressive liberalization, USTR said in a statement. Japan was also motivated by a desire to cut housing costs, it said.
"We are pleased that Japan has promptly implemented its commitment to permit importation of U.S. grademarked lumber," said Charlene Barshefsky, President Clinton's nominee as Trade Representative.
Japan's recognition of visually graded U.S. lumber will enable more than 1,000 mills to ship lumber to Japan, USTR said. Until now, only 80 specially certified U.S. mills could ship lumber to Japan.
Japan is already the largest U.S. export market for wood products, with softwood lumber exports of $619 million in 1995.
